stem: A proton passes undeflected through crossed fields $E=1.6\times10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$ and $B_1=0.08\ \text{T}$, both perpendicular to its velocity. It then enters a uniform field $B_2=0.10\ \text{T}$ at $60^\circ$ to its velocity. Find its displacement magnitude after half a revolution. Take $m_p=1.6\times10^{-27}\ \text{kg}$ and $e=1.6\times10^{-19}\ \text{C}$.

verdicts.working: The selector gives v=E/B₁=2.0×10⁵ m/s. In B₂, v∥=v/2 and v⊥=√3v/2; the half-period is πmₚ/(eB₂)=π×10⁻⁷ s. The parallel displacement is π cm, while the perpendicular displacement is the orbit diameter, 2√3 cm. The total displacement is √(π²+12) cm.

working:
$v=E/B_1=2.0\times10^5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
$\omega=eB_2/m_p=1.0\times10^7\ \text{s}^{-1}$; half-period $\Delta t=\pi/\omega$.
$d_{\parallel}=v\cos60^\circ\,\Delta t=\pi\ \text{cm}$.
$r=v\sin60^\circ/\omega=\sqrt{3}\ \text{cm}$, so $d_{\perp}=2r=2\sqrt{3}\ \text{cm}$.
$d=\sqrt{d_{\parallel}^2+d_{\perp}^2}=\sqrt{\pi^2+12}\ \text{cm}$.

Independent check: The selector gives v=E/B₁=2.0×10⁵ m/s. In B₂, v∥=v/2 and v⊥=√3v/2; the half-period is πmₚ/(eB₂)=π×10⁻⁷ s. The parallel displacement is π cm, while the perpendicular displacement is the orbit diameter, 2√3 cm. The total displacement is √(π²+12) cm.
solution: For undeflected motion, $v=E/B_1=2.0\times10^5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. In $B_2$, the half-period is $\Delta t=\pi m_p/(eB_2)=\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{s}$; hence $d_{\parallel}=v\cos60^\circ\,\Delta t=\pi\ \text{cm}$. The perpendicular displacement is the orbit diameter, $d_{\perp}=2v\sin60^\circ/\omega=2\sqrt3\ \text{cm}$, where $\omega=eB_2/m_p$. Therefore, $d=\sqrt{d_{\parallel}^2+d_{\perp}^2}=\sqrt{\pi^2+12}\ \text{cm}$.

B: uses only the diameter of the circular motion.
D: uses the full-period parallel displacement instead of the half-period displacement.
